=== STEP 2 — DOCS VERIFIED against trino.io/docs/467 via WebFetch on 2026-06-08 ===
  (a) [trino.io/docs/467/functions/comparison.html] — LIKE predicate confirmed: supports ONLY `%` (zero-or-more chars) and `_` (exactly one char), plus optional `ESCAPE` clause. NO bracket character classes `[...]` documented. Square brackets are LITERAL characters when they appear in a LIKE pattern. Bracket-class syntax `[0-9]` / `[a-z]` is a SQL Server T-SQL extension, NOT in Trino.
  (b) [trino.io/docs/467/functions/regexp.html] — Trino regex support is provided EXCLUSIVELY via NAMED FUNCTIONS. Complete Trino 467 list: regexp_count(string,pattern)->bigint, regexp_extract(string,pattern[,group])->varchar, regexp_extract_all(string,pattern[,group])->array<varchar>, regexp_like(string,pattern)->boolean, regexp_position(string,pattern[,start[,occurrence]])->integer, regexp_replace(string,pattern[,replacement|function])->varchar, regexp_split(string,pattern)->array<varchar>. NO `~`/`~*`/`!~`/`!~*` infix regex operators in the docs. NO `RLIKE` function. NO `REGEXP` function. NO `SIMILAR TO`. The named-function list is the entire regex API.
  (c) Pattern syntax = Java pattern syntax (per docs verbatim: 'All of the regular expression functions use the Java pattern syntax'). NOT RE2J as my pre-write working note guessed — CORRECTION made before writing. Inside the pattern string: `^`, `$`, `.`, `\d`, `\w`, `\s`, `[0-9]`, `[a-z]`, `[^xyz]`, `{n}`, `{n,}`, `{n,m}`, `+`, `*`, `?`, `|`, `()`, `(?i)`, POSIX classes `[[:digit:]]` all valid.
  (d) `\d`-vs-`[0-9]` inside a single-quoted SQL string: docs example shows `'\\d+'` (double-backslash) — i.e. `\d` inside a single-quoted SQL string literal IS brittle (downstream tooling — dbt Jinja, Python f-strings, shell heredocs, JDBC drivers, JSON-encoded payloads — frequently consume one backslash level before Trino sees the literal). `[0-9]{8}` avoids ALL backslash-escaping concerns and reads identically through every layer. CONFIRMS the directive's instruction to use `[0-9]` (not `\d`) as the copy-attractive lead form.
  (e) regexp_like is 2-arg ONLY in Trino 467 (no 3-arg flag form; the Oracle `regexp_like(s, pat, 'i')` flag-arg signature is NOT in Trino — see r27:1109 row). The case-insensitive form is the `(?i)` inline-flag-inside-the-pattern style.
